definitions.explanation: A sensation of spinning, unsteadiness, or feeling faint, often accompanied by loss of balance.

examples.japanese: {急|きゅう}に{立|た}ち{上|あ}がったら{眩暈|めまい}がした。
examples.english: I felt dizzy when I stood up suddenly.

examples.japanese: {眩暈|めまい}がして{倒|たお}れそうになった。
examples.english: I felt so dizzy that I nearly collapsed.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}{眩暈|めまい}がひどいので{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to the hospital because my dizziness has been bad lately.

notes:
{眩暈|めまい} (also written as 目眩 or just めまい) refers to dizziness or vertigo.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {眩暈|めまい}がする: to feel dizzy
- {眩暈|めまい}を{起|お}こす: to become dizzy
- {眩暈|めまい}がひどい: to have severe dizziness
- {眩暈|めまい}を{感|かん}じる: to feel dizziness

TYPES OF DIZZINESS:
- {回転性|かいてんせい}{眩暈|めまい}: rotational vertigo (spinning sensation)
- {浮動性|ふどうせい}{眩暈|めまい}: floating dizziness
- {立|た}ちくらみ: lightheadedness when standing

CAUSES:
- {貧血|ひんけつ}: anemia
- {低血圧|ていけつあつ}: low blood pressure
- {疲労|ひろう}: fatigue
- {内耳|ないじ}の{問題|もんだい}: inner ear problems

WRITING NOTE: Often written in hiragana (めまい) in everyday use.
